decks.title: Equations of motion — when to use
decks.subject: physics

cards.front: The question never mentions displacement s
The question never mentions final velocity v
The question never mentions time t
The question never mentions acceleration a
When are the equations of motion valid?
cards.back: Only when the acceleration is uniform (constant). Constant velocity, a = 0, counts.

cards.front: What do you use when the acceleration is NOT uniform?
cards.back: The area under the velocity–time graph. The equations of motion do not apply.

cards.front: The method for choosing an equation
cards.back: List s, u, v, a, t. Mark the three you know and the one you want. The leftover letter is the one to avoid — pick the equation without it.

cards.front: Newton’s first law
cards.back: An object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion continues at constant velocity, unless a resultant force acts on it.

cards.front: Newton’s second law
cards.back: The resultant force on an object equals the product of its mass and its acceleration, and the object accelerates in the direction of the resultant force. Fᴿ = ma

cards.front: Newton’s third law
cards.back: If body A exerts a force on body B, then body B exerts an equal and opposite force on body A.

cards.front: Inertia
cards.back: The reluctance of a body to change its state of rest or motion. It is quantified by the mass of the object.

cards.front: The four tests for an action–reaction pair
cards.back:
Equal in magnitude · opposite in direction · acting on different bodies · of the same nature.
(MOBS)

cards.front: Weight
cards.back:
The gravitational force acting on an object that has mass.
W = mg · newtons · vector

cards.front: Gravitational field strength, g
cards.back:
The gravitational force per unit mass placed at that point.
N kg⁻¹ · about 10 N kg⁻¹ on Earth

cards.front: Friction
cards.back: The force that opposes, or tends to oppose, relative motion between two surfaces in contact.

cards.front: Normal contact force
cards.back: The push exerted by a surface on an object pressing on it. Always perpendicular to the surface.

cards.front: What does a free-body diagram show?
cards.back: The object, and only the forces acting ON it. Forces the object exerts on anything else must not appear.

cards.front: Forces are balanced — what follows?
cards.back: Resultant force = 0 N, so acceleration = 0 m s⁻². The object is either at rest, or moving in a straight line at constant speed.

cards.front: The six energy stores
cards.back: Kinetic · gravitational potential · elastic potential · chemical potential · internal · nuclear

cards.front: The four transfer pathways
cards.back: Mechanically, by a force over a distance · by heating · by propagation of waves · electrically

cards.front: Which common words are NOT energy stores?
cards.back: Heat, light, sound and electricity. They are energy in transit — pathways, not stores.

cards.front: Principle of conservation of energy
cards.back: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred from one store to another. The total energy of an isolated system is constant.

cards.front: Work done
cards.back:
The product of the force and the distance moved in the direction of the force.
W = Fs · joules · scalar

cards.front: When is the work done by a force zero?
cards.back: When the distance moved in the direction of that force is zero — for example carrying a bag horizontally does no work against gravity.

cards.front: Energy in the kinetic store
cards.back: Eᴋ = ½mv² — only the speed is squared

cards.front: Energy in the gravitational potential store
cards.back: Eᴘ = mgh — h measured from the chosen reference level

cards.front: Power
cards.back:
The work done, or energy transferred, per unit time.
P = W ÷ t · watts · scalar

cards.front: The second formula for power
cards.back: P = Fv — a powerful machine is both strong and fast

cards.front: Efficiency
Why is efficiency never 100%?
cards.back: Some energy is always transferred to the internal store of the surroundings, through friction and resistance.

cards.front: Ammonia NH₃

cards.front: Chlorine Cl₂

cards.front: Sulfur dioxide SO₂
